items.title: Multi-tenant support for divergent tenant schemas

labels.name: .Team/UXWest
labels.description: UX West - use for bugs and feature requests

items.body:
**What problem will this feature request solve?**

The current multi-tenant tooling assumes one of following data shapes:
* Per-tenant databases with identical schemas with db routing
* A single multi-tenant database with row-level security / sandboxing
* A singel multi-tenant database with impersonation

Each shape assumes identical tenant schemas, while some customers might see their tenant schemas diverge: a shared "generic" schema plus small per-tenant or per-version customizations (a few tenant specific tables, columns or an extra schema with customer controlled data).

These customers are forced into an all-manual workflow: hand-managing groups, collections, permissions, and serialization across their tenants and databases.


**Describe the solution you'd like.**

Extend the tenant tooling, db routing, db permissions  so a common schema can be shared across tenants while allowing controlled per-tenant divergence, without hand-templatizing everything through serialization. 

Two complementary directions (either would materially help; ideally both):

*Option A — Hybrid database routing (shared schema + per-tenant additions).*
Keep the shared "generic" schema managed once on the primary/template database and fanned out to all tenants as today, but let each destination database **catalog and expose its own tenant-specific tables / sub-schemas** on top of the shared template. In short: routing that tolerates a superset schema per tenant instead of requiring byte-for-byte identical schemas.

*Option B — Per-tenant database tagging (scoped connections).*
Allow a database connection to be **tagged to one or more specific tenants**. A tagged database is queryable only by the listed tenants and is invisible to all others. This gives a clean, declarative way to attach a tenant's divergent/custom data as its own connection while the shared datasets stay common — instead of encoding the isolation manually via groups, collections, and permission grants. It extends primitives the [tenants model](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/embedding/tenants#data-permissions-for-tenants) already exposes: the system-defined `@tenant.slug` attribute is the natural tag key, and the existing **All tenant users** / per-tenant groups are the natural scope — so a tagged database simply grants data access to the listed tenant(s) and is hidden from the rest.


**How does this feature request impact you?**

Request from a Pro / Enterprise trialer


**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Options explored with the customer before filing this (all workable but insufficient at scale):

- **Database routing (identical-schema model)** — doesn't fit: routing syncs only the primary DB and assumes identical schemas, so per-tenant custom tables are dropped.
Customers would need to resort to using native questions or models to query their custom schemas, and some native features such as linked filters, drop-down values would not work. 

- **Tenants feature** — built as convenience sugar over the permission system for the two shapes above. 
Tenant data permissions are assigned via the **All tenant users** group plus the per-tenant groups and cross-tenant segregation is enforced via db routing (separate DBs) *or* a shared DB with Row/Column Security or Impersonation. 
None of these paths can represent a per-tenant schema that diverges from a shared template.

- **Manual groups + collections + per-tenant permissions, templatized via serialization blueprints and the API (the pragmatic path chosen)** — functional, but all-manual: it fans out configuration across hundreds of databases, multiplies the metadata sync surface (tables × columns × tenants), and offers no migration path to a first-class feature later. 
It also surfaces adjacent scale pain — per-tenant database connections.


**Additional context about the requestor**

- Deployment: Metabase Cloud, BigQuery data warehouse, tenant data is located in separate BQ projects or datasets. The theme of the request applies to any dwh type equally.
- Topology per tenant: one shared "generic" schema (identical across all tenants) + one "custom" schema (per-tenant divergence).
- Adjacent concerns the customer raised that this feature would relieve: scalability of hundreds of database connections, and the flat/non-searchable admin Databases UI at that scale.
- The customer explicitly asked whether to **wait for a proper feature or continue the manual serialization approach** . Once implemented, a migration path from the manual/serialization world into a first-class model would be valuable.

items.title: GAS-ROADMAP-002 — Competitor-informed evergreen capability roadmap
items.body:
Status: OWNER-DIRECTED / EVERGREEN INTERNAL R&D PROGRAM
Owner: G.A.S. Product Orchestrator (current repo instructions: Product ORCH2)
Portfolio parent: LowcountryDigitalWorks/business-operations#280
Priority: P1 long-running internal product capability
Cost Class: $0 / included / low-cost first
External commercialization: service-first and separately validated; internal product development is NOT blocked on buyer demand

# GAS-ROADMAP-002 — Competitor-informed evergreen capability roadmap

## Owner direction — 2026-09-29

Lowcountry Digital Works will continue developing G.A.S. Engine as a long-running internal Search / SEO / AI-visibility intelligence product even when immediate customer demand is not yet proven.

The commercial gate and the internal R&D gate are intentionally different:
- Internal R&D may continue because LDW itself benefits from a stronger search/visibility operating system and the owner explicitly wants this as an ongoing strategic development project.
- External managed service may use accepted G.A.S. capabilities through business-operations #280 and continue buyer/service validation.
- External SaaS/customer software remains separately gated by real demand, support/security/privacy burden, customer ownership, and commercial evidence.

Do not use lack of current buyer proof as a reason to freeze useful internal capability development.
Do not use this direction as permission to build a large multi-tenant SaaS, crawler, dashboard stack, custom auth, paid data warehouse, or autonomous publishing system without a separate gate.

## North star

Build a provider-neutral evidence and decision-support system that helps LDW repeatedly answer:
1. What changed?
2. Where is visibility improving or degrading?
3. Why is the change likely happening?
4. Which opportunities are material enough to act on?
5. What bounded action should be proposed?
6. What changed after the action?
7. What should remain monitored?

Lifecycle:
OBSERVE -> NORMALIZE -> COMPARE -> CORRELATE -> DETECT -> PRIORITIZE -> RECOMMEND -> HUMAN/OWNER APPROVAL WHEN REQUIRED -> ACT THROUGH SEPARATELY AUTHORIZED PATH -> REMEASURE -> REPORT OUTCOME

## Competitive-research method

Perform a deep capability-by-capability competitor review before each material G.A.S. expansion.
Do NOT clone vendors or copy proprietary implementations.

For every capability domain:
1. identify the best current specialists / OSS / major-platform features;
2. document the user problem they solve;
3. document inputs, outputs, cadence, and decision model;
4. identify what is commodity sensing vs differentiated interpretation/workflow;
5. choose BUILD / INTEGRATE / CONFIGURE / WATCH / DO NOT PURSUE;
6. estimate recurring cost, support burden, privacy/security burden, and customer-data implications;
7. define the smallest internal proof using LDW-owned/public-safe evidence;
8. implement only after the Product Orchestrator freezes a bounded release.

## Capability domains to research

### A. Search Console analytics / Google search intelligence
References: GSC Wizard, Google Search Console native API/export, SEOTesting-class experiment systems.
Candidate capabilities: striking-distance/page-poaching opportunities; query/page decay; CTR underperformance; cannibalization; brand/non-brand segmentation; content/topic grouping; date-window comparisons; URL inspection/indexing health; anomaly/change-point signals; annotations and before/after measurement.

### B. Query intent / page-focus / content architecture
References: GSC Wizard query-shape analysis; MarketMuse/Clearscope/Surfer/Frase/InLinks; major SEO-suite keyword/topic clustering.
Candidate capabilities: detect one URL serving materially different intent clusters; distinguish consolidation vs split-page opportunities; page/query-cluster mapping; content-gap and supporting-topic evidence; internal-link target suggestions.
Owner-supplied 2026-09-28 GSC Wizard email is design evidence: reverse cannibalization can identify one page collecting unrelated query clusters; split only when each new page can become a real unique page; keep the original URL for its primary intent; compare SERPs/competitors before declaring intents distinct.

### C. Multi-engine indexing/crawl triangulation
References: Google Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools/AI Performance, Yandex Webmaster, IndexNow.
Candidate capabilities: compare indexing/crawl state across engines; distinguish site-wide technical breakage from engine-specific behavior; preserve per-engine freshness/coverage windows; detect inconsistent canonical/index states; record IndexNow submission/indexing observations without treating Bing/Yandex ranking as a proxy for Google.

### D. Technical SEO / site quality
References: WQT, SiteOne, Lighthouse, Screaming Frog, Sitebulb, Ahrefs Site Audit, Semrush Site Audit.
Candidate G.A.S. role: consume normalized technical evidence; preserve semantic magnitudes/trends/provenance; correlate technical changes with search/visibility outcomes; do not rebuild a crawler.

### E. AI / answer-engine visibility
References: ZeroRank plus Profound/Peec/Scrunch/Otterly-class platforms and Bing Copilot visibility.
Candidate capabilities: prompt/brand visibility trends; citation/source coverage; source-URL concentration; competitive mention gaps; visibility change after bounded site/content changes; provenance and prompt-cohort consistency.

### F. Rank / SERP / competitor intelligence
References: Ahrefs, Semrush, SE Ranking, Moz, DataForSEO-class providers.
Candidate stance: avoid building a rank crawler; use native/free/vendor data only where it materially improves decisions; preserve source/freshness/coverage and do not blend unlike rank universes into one proprietary score.

### G. Local SEO / local business visibility
References: Google Business Profile; BrightLocal/Whitespark/Local Falcon-class tools.
Candidate capabilities: GBP completeness/visibility evidence; local query/landing-page opportunities; review/reputation linkage where separately authorized; local-pack/grid data only when a low-cost source proves useful.

### H. Links / authority / internal linking
References: Ahrefs/Majestic/Moz; GSC links data; crawler-derived internal-link graph.
Candidate capabilities: internal-link opportunity scoring from existing site graph + search demand; backlink change evidence only if an affordable authoritative source exists; no custom internet-scale backlink crawler.

### I. SEO experimentation / annotations / outcomes
References: SEOTesting; Search Console annotations/change logs; statistical experimentation systems.
Candidate capabilities: change annotations; bounded pre/post cohorts; same-source remeasurement; outcome confidence/not-yet-measurable state; avoid causal claims when only correlation is supported.

### J. Reporting / operator workflow
References: GSC Wizard reports/MCP; Looker Studio/AgencyAnalytics-class reporting; accepted G.A.S. operator case view.
Candidate capabilities: deterministic compact metrics before LLM interpretation; source/freshness/unit/window attached to every derived fact; maximum-three-priority customer summary; deeper operator detail separate from customer view; MCP/read-only API only when repeated operator friction justifies it.

## Cross-cutting design principles learned from GSC Wizard
1. Heavy arithmetic/aggregation happens deterministically before model interpretation.
2. Models receive compact finished metrics, not huge raw Search Console row dumps.
3. Every signal carries source, period, freshness, coverage, units, filters and provenance.
4. Preserve API-specific reporting lag instead of manufacturing zeroes for missing days.
5. Filters such as brand/content group/topic cluster are typed dimensions, not ad hoc prose.
6. Connected-provider errors distinguish permission/property/verification problems from generic reconnect advice.
7. Multi-engine evidence is comparative diagnosis, not score blending.
8. Recommendations are grounded in measured evidence and rechecked after implementation.

## Immediate research + roadmap output
Create a living competitor matrix in the repository with: capability; user job/problem; leading products/platforms; useful patterns; commodity vs differentiated; BUILD/INTEGRATE/WATCH/SKIP; data source/credential implications; recurring cost; privacy/security; smallest proof; candidate G.A.S. release.

Then propose the next three bounded releases, prioritizing reusable internal value over UI breadth.

## Initial likely release sequence — hypothesis until Product Orchestrator freezes it

### Candidate 0.10 — Search Analytics Signal Pack
Pure/deterministic analytics over normalized GSC-like evidence: trend windows; striking-distance; decay; CTR opportunity; cannibalization; brand/non-brand grouping; explicit data-window/freshness semantics. No provider networking required for the first mechanism proof.

### Candidate 0.11 — Intent / Page-Focus Analysis
Provider-neutral page/query-cluster representation and split/consolidate opportunity evidence. No autonomous content generation. No SERP scraping unless separately authorized and justified.

### Candidate 0.12 — Multi-Engine Index Diagnostics
Provider-neutral index/crawl state model that can compare Google/Bing/Yandex-style evidence and classify broad site issue, engine-specific issue, or coverage uncertainty. No rank-score blending.

Later candidates may cover AI-visibility correlation, internal linking, experiment/annotation intelligence, and richer operator workflows.

## Implementation authority
This issue authorizes competitor research and roadmap definition.
Each software release still requires current-main reconciliation, exact release contract, smallest proof, branch/PR, deterministic tests, security/privacy review, independent review, and Product Orchestrator acceptance before merge/next release.
No direct production/customer mutation follows from a G.A.S. recommendation.

## Automation relationship
Automation & Agent Operations owns provider/event ingestion, read-only sensor collection paths, scheduling/event triggers, executor routing, generated evidence handoff, and operational observability.
G.A.S. Product Orchestrator owns domain contracts, normalized semantic model, deterministic analysis, recommendation/measurement/outcome logic, release roadmap, and product acceptance.
business-operations #280 remains the managed-service/commercial application gate.

items.title: [Warehouse] P3-23 · A sandbox practice warehouse with disposable data, and in-product help per screen

labels.name: reopened-e2e
labels.description: Reopened by the WH-E2E / real-world review 2026-11

items.body:
Part of #7 · Module **`warehouse`** · Migrations **—** · Screens **— (help content attaches to every warehouse screen through the platform `HelpButton`)**

**Functional contracts:** [`docs/contracts/non-functional.contract.md`](../docs/contracts/non-functional.contract.md)

## Scope

> **Round-2 addition — `H-010`.** **Mobile row: `none`.** State it explicitly rather than leaving
> the header's `Screens **—**` to imply it — this task ships no screen of its own, so there is no
> mobile counterpart to build and no reader should go looking for one.

- **A sandbox / practice warehouse with disposable data** (`FR-442`). For a warehouse this is not a
  nicety: **you cannot train pickers on live stock**. Every training pick is a real movement in an
  **append-only ledger that has no delete**, so the alternative is a month of reversals with training
  reason codes polluting the adjustment register (`WH-SC-254`).
- **In-product help content per screen**, on the platform's existing help affordance. `HelpButton.tsx`
  is verified present in `platform/frontend/src/components/common/` — it **exists and needs content**
  (`PLATFORM-DEPENDENCIES.md` §1.13, `S-094`).
- The sandbox is a **flagged warehouse whose data is disposable**, not a second database and not a
  second install: `OD-3` keeps one database per customer, so a parallel environment is a parallel
  customer.

## How the sandbox is shaped, and what it must not be

- **It is a `whb_warehouses` row carrying a sandbox flag**, and every movement in it is an ordinary
  movement with that warehouse's id. That is what makes it disposable *and* realistic: the operator
  learns the real screens, the real scans and the real refusals.
- **Every report, valuation, statistics strip, export and accounting handover excludes it by
  predicate.** This is the load-bearing half. The accounting set learned it as
  `acc_companies.is_rehearsal`: *reports written before the flag exists include rehearsal data with
  no predicate to exclude it.*
- **Disposal is a purge of that warehouse's rows, not a ledger delete.** `L-2`/`L-3` hold everywhere
  else in the product; the sandbox's exemption is that its whole warehouse can be dropped, and that
  exemption is stated in one place rather than discovered as a delete path on the ledger service.

## Requirements closed
`FR-442`

## Scenarios closed
`WH-SC-254` (six new pickers and ₹4 crore of live stock: they train in a sandbox with disposable
data and in-product help per screen)

## Closes
`S-094` · `H-010`


## Traps

- **The flag must exist before the first movement, or the exclusion predicate has nothing to read.**
  This is a `PNR-3`-class problem in miniature: a sandbox warehouse identified retroactively means
  every report already run included training data and nobody can say which figures were affected.
  The flag belongs on `whb_warehouses` (`P1-05`, `V500012`) — if it is not there when this task
  starts, adding it is a **new migration in the base band**, and every report predicate is amended in
  the same task.
- **A purge is not a `DELETE` on the ledger service.** `L-2` and `L-3` make movements append-only and
  immutable and there is deliberately no delete path. The sandbox purge is a maintenance operation
  scoped to one warehouse id, permissioned, audited, and it does **not** open a general delete method
  on the writer service. One escape hatch on the ledger becomes the way a support engineer "fixes"
  production.
- **Do not train with real reason codes.** Training movements posted into the live warehouse with a
  `TRAINING` reason code are `WH-SC-254`'s named failure: they pollute the adjustment register, they
  reach the Rule 56 statutory categories (`P4-03`) and they are then part of a filed return.
- **Help content is en / fr / hi**, registered in the module SafeTranslation. `S-095`: warehouse
  operators are the most language-diverse users in the suite.
- **`HelpButton` exists — do not build a second help affordance.** `/preflight-check` before writing
  any component; the platform component set is verified present at
  `platform/frontend/src/components/common/HelpButton.tsx`.
- **The sandbox is not a demo dataset.** A seeded fixture that cannot be reset is used once and then
  abandoned; the requirement is **disposable**, which means resettable on demand.
- **Exclusion applies to the accounting handover too** (`D-6`): a sandbox movement handed over to
  accounting is a journal in a real ledger, and `posting_status` will happily carry it.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A sandbox warehouse exists, an operator completes a full receive→putaway→pick→pack→ship cycle in it, and the movements are ordinary ledger movements
- [ ] Every report, valuation, statistics strip and export **excludes** the sandbox by predicate, verified on at least the position report, the valuation report and the movement register
- [ ] No sandbox movement reaches the accounting handover
- [ ] The sandbox resets on demand, by a permissioned and audited purge scoped to one warehouse id
- [ ] The ledger writer service gains **no** delete method, and `L-2`/`L-3` still hold for every other warehouse
- [ ] Training produces **zero** rows in the live adjustment register
- [ ] Every warehouse screen has help content behind the existing `HelpButton`, in en / fr / hi
- [ ] No second help component is created
- [ ] **Scenarios** `WH-SC-254`

## Reopened scope (WH-E2E review, 2026-11-03)

Found by the 2026-11-03 end-to-end review (code at classic HEAD 4843b1648d, plus the real-world check). This issue cannot close until each item below is met.

### W02-05 · Exclude sandbox sites from India statutory outputs and e-way bills (major, CLOSED-INCOMPLETE)

> **Statutory content.** Sources are cited under Evidence; anything marked UNVERIFIED there, and every figure, must be confirmed against the law in force at build time.

#### Why this matters

Practice-warehouse stock is counted in the Form 3CD quantitative statement and the GSTIN stock account, so a tax auditor or GST officer sees training stock as real; a sandbox delivery challan can raise a real e-way bill on the government portal.

#### Scope

Apply the sandbox predicate to Form 3CD, statutory stock account, ITC-04/EPR/Schedule H1/bonded register ledger reads; refuse (422) e-way bill generate/consolidate and transfer IRN for a sandbox site in service and DB guard; contract test coverage for warehouse-india.

#### Acceptance

- A receipt in a sandbox site of company C does not change C's Form 3CD figures
- A GSTIN stock account period excludes lines of a sandbox site linked to the same branch
- E-way bill generation for a sandbox challan returns 422 with no provider call or api-log row
- A contract test fails when a warehouse-india repository reads ledger history without the sandbox predicate

#### Evidence (classic HEAD 4843b1648d, 2026-11-03)

in warehouse-india/backend/src/main only WhinStockByMrpRepositoryCustomImpl reads is_sandbox/WhbSandboxScope; WhinForm3cdRunRepositoryCustomImpl.java:42-52 no site predicate; WhinStockAccountPeriodRepositoryCustomImpl.java:285-298 sites by GSTIN, no sandbox check; WhinEwayBillService.java:204,224 no sandbox refusal. P3-23 acceptance: every report and export excludes the sandbox.

items.title: E1.11 Data conventions
items.body:
As a customer, I want one installation per company with strict per-site separation so my warehouses' data never mixes and my supervisors see only their sites.

### Acceptance criteria

- Single-tenant per install (one company per database; no tenant_id). A hosted offering would be siloed: one database and one Kubernetes namespace per customer.
- Unit of work = one DbContext per request/job (behind `IUnitOfWork`); single `SaveChanges` per operation; explicit transactions only for listed multi-step operations (deposit replay, marriage, intake, settings cascade, lease release/expiry) and kept free of non-database I/O; no distributed transactions (outbox carries side effects); read-committed isolation.
- Data access: repository per aggregate (not per table) — a specific interface per aggregate (`ISkuRepository`, `IZoneGroupRepository`, `IReleaseRepository`, …) inheriting the generic base interfaces `IReadOnlyRepository<T,TId>`, `ISearchableRepository<T>`, `IWriteOnlyRepository<T>` (candidate for a `Wolfgang.Repositories` library) and adding the few business-named methods that need EF (`GetForUpdateAsync`, `GetByBarcodeAsync`, `GetChangedSinceAsync`); master-data CRUD comes from the base for free. Repositories fetch and persist aggregates; handlers own orchestration and rules; cross-aggregate work is a handler using several repositories inside one `IUnitOfWork`.
- `IUnitOfWork` is a thin seam over `DbContext` — `SaveChangesAsync` and `ExecuteInTransactionAsync(Func<…>)` only (delegate form so rollback and EF retry are automatic); no `Set<T>()`, no change-tracker access. Handlers reference repositories and `IUnitOfWork`, never `DbContext` (architecture test); repository interfaces never expose `IQueryable`, `DbContext`, or expression-tree search (criteria objects only, AOT-safe).
- Reads for screens and reports stay separate: query classes projecting to records, not repositories — the place where Dapper is benchmarked (E36.5). Handler unit tests use fakes of the repository interfaces; DbContextBuilder tests the EF repositories themselves.
- `site_id` on all site-scoped entities with an EF global query filter from the caller's site context; cross-site reads require `IgnoreQueryFilters()` behind a permission; writes outside scope rejected at `SaveChanges`; global tables (users, roles, global settings, SKUs, barcodes, license) unfiltered; `site_id` leads most indexes.

items.title: [Warehouse] EPIC: Warehouse and inventory management — master
items.body:
> **Re-target — [`DECISIONS.md` `D-16`](../docs/DECISIONS.md) (2026-10-22), [R28](../docs/reviews/R28-manufacturing-storage-retarget-impact.md) §8b.** The product
> serves **manufacturing plant stores + storage**; dealer and retail/e-commerce code are removed, the
> dealer and services adapters are not rebuilt, and two modules are added (`warehouse-trade`,
> `warehouse-manufacturing`). Four phases are added and run **`P7` → `P8` → {`P9`, `P10`}** (table below).
> **VOID tasks:** `P2-24` #149 · `P2-25` #150 · `P2-26` #151 · `P3-19` #95 · `P5-12` #67 · `P5-15` #81 ·
> `P6-09` #134. **Partially VOID:** `P3-18` #90 · `P5-08` #48 · `P5-09` #52 · `P5-11` #62 · `P5-13` #72 ·
> `P5-23` #123. **Superseded:** `P6-12` #144 (BOM → `warehouse-manufacturing`). The counts and the
> D-11 / D-13 / OD-2 rows below predate `D-16`; `DECISIONS.md` wins.

Build a **standalone-capable, country-neutral warehouse and inventory-management product** for the
Classic platform, as **five Maven modules plus adapters**.

Design set: **`neetub1508/warehouse-issues`** — read order at the bottom of this page. Code lands in
**`neetub1508/classic`**.

> **Seven audit lenses, 2026-09-01.** The live `classic` checkout, the in-flight `accounting` design set,
> and 28,928 lines of prior warehouse / supply-chain / TMS design art → **575 findings** across
> `reviews/R1`–`R7`, 11,750 lines. `DECISIONS.md` §6 allocates the namespaces: `C-001`…`C-050` (codebase
> reality) · `T-001`…`T-097` (tier-1 WMS) · `E-001`…`E-090` (ERP/mid-market) · `F-001`…`F-093`
> (fulfilment/3PL) · `S-001`…`S-098` (standards/statute) · `P-001`…`P-060` (prior art) ·
> `G-001`…`G-086` (the logistics seam). *(Those seven ranges span 574 ids; the total is 575 because at
> least one finding carries a suffixed id — `T-020a`, cited by `FR-023`. Stated rather than papered over,
> per §7 rule 1.)* Every decision on this page traces to at least one finding, and the namespaces are
> disjoint **by construction** — because *the accounting set's most expensive defect was three different
> things sharing one namespace, which a late rename could not repair.*

## The product in one paragraph

`platform + warehouse-base + warehouse` is a **complete, shippable stock product** — no dealer, no
automotive, no accounting. At its centre is **one immutable, double-sided, append-only stock ledger at
full grain**: every stock event is a movement with two or more lines that conserve quantity, positions are
a **cache** that a full rebuild must reproduce exactly, and a correction is a **reversal** — there is no
edit anywhere in the product. Around it sit the application layers that write to it and a **generic
inbound movement port**, so that any number of future consumers — a logistics/TMS module, a
supply-chain/procurement module, a POS, an eCommerce channel, or any vertical in the suite — can move
stock **without `warehouse-base` ever depending on them**. It is not a replacement for anything currently
shipping: `services`, `field-service` and `assets` have **no** stock capability at all (R1 `C-034`), and
`services.parts_used` is free `TEXT`. It is the first real stock ledger in this suite.

## The five modules

| Module | Java package | Prefix | Flyway band | Depends on | Ships |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`warehouse-base`** | `ai.warehousebase` | **`whb_`** | **V500000–V509999** | **platform only** | v1 |
| **`warehouse`** | `ai.warehouse` | **`wh_`** | **V510000–V519999** | platform + base | v1 |
| **`warehouse-adapter-<vertical>`** | `ai.warehouseadapter<vertical>` — a **sibling**, never `ai.warehouse.adapter.*` | `whad_` dealer · `whas_` services · `whaf_` field-service · `whaa_` assets · `whae_` example | **V520000–V529999**, sub-allocated 1,000 per adapter | platform + base + that vertical | v1 → v1.1 |
| **`warehouse-3pl`** | `ai.warehouse3pl` | **`wh3_`** | **V530000–V539999** | platform + base + app | v2 |
| **`warehouse-india`** | `ai.warehouseindia` | **`whin_`** | **V540000–V549999** | platform + base + app | v1 (documents) + v2 (registers) |
| **`warehouse-trade`** *(D-16)* | `ai.warehousetrade` | **`wht_`** | **V550000–V559999** | platform + base + app | P9 |
| **`warehouse-manufacturing`** *(D-16)* | `ai.warehousemanufacturing` | **`whm_`** | **V560000–V569999** | platform + base + app | P10 |

Reserved since v1 and built in v3: **`logistics`** — package `ai.logistics`, prefix **`log_`**, band
**V524000–V524999**, and the `logistics:*` permission namespace seeded by `WHB-71` (`V501000`).

**The adapter package must be a sibling.** `@ComponentScan("ai.warehouse")` matches by package **prefix**,
so `ai.warehouse.adapter.dealer` would load in **every** install, including ones where dealer is not
built. This is the exact trap the accounting round-4 review found and corrected.

## The fourteen decisions — do not re-litigate these

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| **D-1** | **Five modules, not four.** `warehouse-india` is the fifth and was not in the brief: the brief's four modules carry a *vertical* axis and **no jurisdiction axis**, so every India rule would otherwise live in `warehouse` (unsellable outside India) or in an adapter (invisible to a pharma customer). Accounting took the same decision and shipped `accounting-india` |

## The fourteen load-bearing invariants

Each has **a database guard and a service guard**. The service guard rejects **first, in the transaction,
with a field-level error**; the database guard is the backstop for the paths the service does not own.
**A trigger firing in production is an incident, not a validation.**

| # | Invariant | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| **L-1** | **Conservation** — every movement's lines sum to zero in base UoM per (owner, item, lot, serial, duty status), balancing against a **virtual location**, never against nothing | Without it a "receipt" can create stock from nowhere and no rebuild will ever tie |
| **L-2** | **Append-only** — no posted line is ever `UPDATE`d or `DELETE`d. Three layers: one writer service with no update method, a `to_jsonb`-diff trigger rejecting `INSERT` into a posted movement as well as `UPDATE`/`DELETE`, and no repository path | Two layers is one bug away from a mutable ledger. The trigger protects later-added columns automatically |
| **L-3** | **Correction is reversal** — mirrored lines, a mandatory reason code from the catalogue, the original marked reversed. **"Edit" is never offered anywhere in the product** | It erodes under *"just let the storekeeper fix it"* pressure, which is why it is written as a product rule, not a service rule |
| **L-4** | **Positions are a cache** — a full rebuild from `whb_stock_movements` reproduces every position row **exactly**, proved nightly with a drift alert | It is the only thing that makes the ledger the truth rather than a second opinion |
| **L-5** | **Full-grain key** — (company, owner, item, location, lot, serial, lpn, stock_status, duty_status). **Every column exists in v1 even where its feature ships later** | A key member added after the ledger has rows is a re-key of the hottest table in the product |
| **L-6** | **Negative available is refused; negative on-hand is a policy** — `available = on_hand − Σ open reservations` may never go below zero; physical on-hand may only where an explicit per-item × per-site policy allows | The accessories code comment names the exact race its Java read-compare-write does not win |
| **L-7** | **Quantity is in base UoM with the conversion factor frozen on the line** | A ledger that re-derives from today's factor **silently restates last year** |
| **L-8** | **Period-bound** — a movement into a locked period is refused, **including a reversal**; a soft close needs an approved override, a hard close admits nothing | It is what makes a closed period mean something to an auditor |
| **L-9** | **Ingestion is idempotent** — `(source_system, idempotency_key)` unique; a repeat returns the original and posts nothing. **The key is never server-generated** | An already-double-posted ledger cannot be deduplicated afterwards: the duplicate is indistinguishable from a legitimate repeat |
| **L-10** | **Allocation is an open-item ledger, not a counter** — every reservation is a row with a holder quad and an `expires_at` | With a counter you cannot release **one** order's hold, and the only repair is to zero it — which releases everyone's |
| **L-11** | **Ownership never changes silently** — a title transfer is an explicit movement type with its own reason code. Goods can change owner without moving, and move without changing owner | Whose a unit is, is a contractual fact, not a derived one |
| **L-12** | **Traceability is reconstructible in both directions** — forward *(where did this lot go)* and backward *(what went into this unit)*, for the full retention period, **across the kit boundary** | A recall is retrospective by definition; genealogy not captured at the moment of transformation can never be acquired |
| **L-13** | **Three timestamps, never one** — `occurred_at` (when it physically happened, producer-supplied), `recorded_at` (when we heard), `posting_date` (the accounting date) | One timestamp cannot be split later, and collapsing them kills offline replay, degraded-mode catch-up, cut-off and EPCIS **simultaneously** |
| **L-14** | **Non-own stock is never valued** — `owner_type != OWN` hands over for quantity and custody reporting only; what we carry is a custody liability and an insured value, **a different number on a different report** | A 3PL that posts its clients' stock to its own balance sheet has a catastrophe in both directions |

Each is a **merge gate on a named task**, not a note.

> ## ⛔ `OD-10` HAS THE TIGHTEST DEADLINE IN THE PROGRAMME

> **Is MRP a dimension of the stock position?** It must be answered **before `P0-02` writes migration
> `V500030`** — the file that sets the position unique key **and, in the same file, seals the ledger

## Migration discipline

| Module | Band |
|---|---|
| `warehouse-base` | **V500000 – V509999** |
| `warehouse` | **V510000 – V519999** |
| `warehouse-adapter-*` (shared, sub-allocated 1,000 per adapter: dealer V520000, services V521000, field-service V522000, assets V523000, **logistics V524000**) | **V520000 – V529999** |
| `warehouse-3pl` | **V530000 – V539999** |
| `warehouse-india` | **V540000 – V549999** |

- **Exactly one task owns each number**, pre-allocated in that task's header, inside its module's band, so
  parallel work cannot collide. A task needing a second file takes the next number **inside its own
  block**, never the next globally free one. A number is never reused even if its task is dropped.
- **Never invent a number that looks plausible.** An early draft cited `V510126` for `wh_tracking_links`;
  the table is `WH-109` at `V510209`. It was caught before publication and recorded, because *"an invented
  migration number that looks plausible is precisely the failure mode `DECISIONS.md` §7 rule 3 exists to
  prevent."*
- **Every migration is individually idempotent** (`IF NOT EXISTS` / `ON CONFLICT` / `WHERE NOT EXISTS`).
  `FlywayConfiguration.java:246-264` runs a blind `flyway.repair()` and one retry on **any** failure, so a
  partially-failed migration **re-runs**.
- **Two shared files are not migrations and are the highest merge-conflict surface in the plan:**
  `platform/frontend/src/utils/filterUtils.ts` (213 scopes — a field absent from its scope is **silently
  dropped** before the request is built) and `CacheConfiguration.java` (234 names — an unregistered name
  throws on the **first call, not at startup**). Batch their edits.
- **The grid config table is `filter_definitions`** (`platform/…/V229:8`). **`grid_filter_definitions`
  does not exist** and inserting into that name crash-loops the backend.

## Definition of done — every task in every phase

`/grill` before any code, with the canonical reference named (Department / Customer / Service Vehicle) and
**diffed against it** · **`reviewer` agent**: zero load-bearing and zero parity findings ·
**`functional-reviewer` in conformance mode** against the matching contract in `docs/contracts/`, authored
in the task if the workflow has none · **the `WH-SC-nnn` scenarios the task claims are walked in the
running app**, not reasoned about · migration idempotent, forward-only, never edited in place, number
owned by exactly one task, carrying `IRREVERSIBLE.md` §3.6's four-question header comment · permissions
granted with the `role_permissions` back-fill in the same migration, `permission_dependencies` rows
**`INSERT`ed, never `CREATE TABLE`d** (it is a platform table, `V248:17-30`), AUDITOR gets `:view` and
never `:export` · grid ships column definitions, `filter_definitions` **and** `grid_preferences` with
**both** `default_columns` and `default_filters` · filter keys in `COMMON_FILTER_CONFIGS` **and** accepted
by the controller, every as-on/from-to filter authored as **two `date` filters** (there is no `daterange`
type, and `dateOnly` is a distinct type from `date`) · cache names registered — **and filter-aware
statistics registered nowhere** · export a superset of the visible grid columns honouring filters **and
sort** · i18n **en / fr / hi** in the module's SafeTranslation · **mobile counterpart delivered, or its
absence declared with a reason — silence is a defect** · **Docker build requested; there is no local
toolchain, so never run `mvn`, `npm` or `tsc` to "verify"**.

**Five additions specific to this programme:**

1. **A migration that only `RAISE NOTICE`s its checks is not verified.** Assert with `RAISE EXCEPTION`, so
   a future apply against a different database fails loudly.
2. **Every `L-n` invariant has a database guard *and* a service guard**, and the service guard rejects
   **first, in the transaction, with a field-level error**. *A trigger firing in production is an incident,
   not a validation.*
3. **The loose-coupling ratchet runs in CI**, not in a reviewer's memory: `WarehouseBaseCouplingTest`'s six
   assertions, a per-module `ArchitectureInvariantsTest`, and `warehouse-adapter-example` built green, with
   `warehouse-ratchets` running on every PR (required-check setting waived).
4. **Every threshold column ships with the scheduled job that reads it.** *A dated obligation with no actor
   is a defect at the moment it is merged, not when it is noticed.*
5. **A task creating a `status` column ships its ladder rows** in `BUILD-SPEC-SCREENS.md` §0.11, in the same
   PR — `Table | From | To | Verb | Actor (permission) | Guard | Terminal?`. **A state with no inbound
   transition, and a non-terminal state with no outbound transition, are both defects.** Every verb in the
   ladder is a §10.2 permission string, not an `:edit` (`H-004`, `H-001`). *A status value written by a
   build that guessed the ladder is in the customer's table forever, and the `IRR-41`-shaped append-only
   tables cannot be corrected by `UPDATE`.*

**Segments a v1 install cannot serve at all:** pharmaceutical distribution, cold chain, 3PL contract
logistics and eCommerce fulfilment — all v2. Apparel and footwear becomes servable at v2 **because** `A-3`
put the variant schema in v1; had it not, the segment would have been **permanently** declined.

**23 deliberate refusals** (`COMPETITOR-BENCHMARK.md` §7), each with a stated re-entry path and each of
which **must appear in the product documentation in the place a reader would look for the feature** —
*"'Not built, because X' is a credible answer in a sales conversation; silence is not."* Among them: a TMS,
distributed order management, a labour-standards engineering engine, incentive pay, direct automation
control, voice picking, a slotting solver, demand forecasting, LIFO, a general-purpose rules engine or
expression language, JSONB custom-field bags, multi-tenant SaaS, UDI/pharma serialisation regimes, export
and customs documentation, an invoice or tax engine inside `warehouse-3pl`, a consumer returns portal, an
EPCIS repository, retail-compliance EDI, and yard/trailer management.

**The honest one-line summary.** A v1 install is a **correct, auditable, multi-site, multi-owner stock
ledger with a parts catalogue, an Indian-legal movement document set and enough screens for a storekeeper
to run a day** — and it is **not** a warehouse *execution* system, a 3PL platform, a fulfilment platform or
a compliance filing product until v1.1, v2 and v2 respectively.

## Read order for the design set

1. **[`DECISIONS.md`](../blob/main/docs/DECISIONS.md)** — **first, always.** It wins over every other
   document except `reviews/R1`, which wins on any question about what the *existing* codebase does,
   because it carries `file:line` evidence. Module names, packages, bands, prefixes, id namespaces and the
   version ladder are fixed there **and nowhere else**.
2. **[`IRREVERSIBLE.md`](../blob/main/docs/IRREVERSIBLE.md)** — what is free now and impossible later.
3. **[`WAREHOUSE-FUNCTIONAL-REQUIREMENTS.md`](../blob/main/docs/WAREHOUSE-FUNCTIONAL-REQUIREMENTS.md)** —
   the 446 `FR-nnn`, each with its module, version, phase and source findings.
4. **[`DATA-MODEL.md`](../blob/main/docs/DATA-MODEL.md)** — the migration authority: every table (§2), **the
   split proof** (§3 — every boundary-crossing FK and the proof it points downward), the `I-n` enforceable
   constraints (§6), and the allocation (§7).
5. **[`PORT-AND-ADAPTER-CONTRACT.md`](../blob/main/docs/PORT-AND-ADAPTER-CONTRACT.md)** — the wire: the
   envelope, idempotency, **§4 the outbox and its billable granularity**, reservations, the open
   catalogues, the build-time coupling test, and **§9 the consumers**.
6. **[`SCENARIO-CATALOGUE.md`](../blob/main/docs/SCENARIO-CATALOGUE.md)** — **these are the acceptance
   criteria.** "Done" means walked in a running application.
7. **[`BUILD-SPEC-SCREENS.md`](../blob/main/docs/BUILD-SPEC-SCREENS.md)** — the 237 screens, their tables,
   columns, filters, actions and mobile verdicts.
8. **[`IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md`](../blob/main/docs/IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md)** — the 144-task decomposition,
   the critical path, the four points of no return, the open decisions as gates, and the traceability.
9. **[`MODULE-INTEGRATION.md`](../blob/main/docs/MODULE-INTEGRATION.md)** — the **22** integration
   touchpoints, three of which fail **silently**.
10. **[`PLATFORM-DEPENDENCIES.md`](../blob/main/docs/PLATFORM-DEPENDENCIES.md)** ·
    **[`COEXISTENCE.md`](../blob/main/docs/COEXISTENCE.md)** ·
    **[`INDIA-LOCALISATION-PACK.md`](../blob/main/docs/INDIA-LOCALISATION-PACK.md)** ·
    **[`COMPETITOR-BENCHMARK.md`](../blob/main/docs/COMPETITOR-BENCHMARK.md)**.
11. **`reviews/R1`–`R7`** — the 575 findings, when a task's `## Closes` block needs its evidence.
    **`R1` wins on any claim about the live codebase.** And beware **`R2`'s two numbering systems**: its
    capability-matrix rows are numbered independently of its `T-nnn` findings, so a matrix row number reads
    exactly like a finding id and resolves to the wrong thing. **Cite an R2 finding only after opening the
    `T-nnn` heading itself.**

## The rules every author of this design set follows

1. **Never state a count you did not compute with a command.** Put the command in the document.
2. **Every claim about the `classic` codebase carries `file:line`.** If you could not verify it, write
   `UNVERIFIED` and say what would verify it.
3. **Every cross-reference must resolve.** *The accounting set's worst failure was fabricated
   cross-references that looked plausible and resolved to nothing — 25 dangling `FR-nnn` citations of which
   **19 resolved to a different real requirement**, so live gaps read as closed.*
4. **Never blanket search-and-replace an id.** It corrupted the accounting decisions table twice.
5. **The `.md` files are authoritative; GitHub issue bodies are a mirror** kept in sync by
   `issues/create-issues.sh --sync`, with `--check` failing CI on drift. **Never edit an issue body in the
   GitHub UI.**
6. **Do not run `mvn` / `npm` / `tsc`.** This project builds only in Docker. Verification is by reading,
   grep and diff against the canonical references named in CLAUDE.md.
